column3: Near-verbatim parallel: the sign settles hearts while victory remains from God.
Sets an impatient demand for the promised event against the focus's reassuring announcement.
Places divine guidance and aid amid prophetic opposition, without making opposition the final measure.
Directly develops heart-settling through remembrance of God.
Supplies the preceding plea and announced angelic reinforcement behind the sign in 8:10.
Contrasts the focus's divine source with a failed network of mutual support.
Shows unseen reinforcement and tranquility in danger while God remains the decisive helper.
Adds the surrounding conflict in which divine direction overrides hostile planning.
Provides a contrary heart-response test when God alone is mentioned.
Continues the immediate sequence: security, material provision, and strengthening of hearts.
Counters impatience by presenting part of the awaited matter as already close behind.
Frames appeal for help under rejection, leaving the form of response to God.
Only echoes the divine attributes; it adds little to the sign, hearts, and victory relation.
Balances reliance on divine victory with preparation through available means.
Connects revealed input with increased faith and joy, but only indirectly with the focus.
Joins good news with help from God and a near opening.
Repeats the skeptical, delayed-promise posture already supplied by earlier cards.
Affirms powerful divine help, while its contrary route remains boundary evidence.
Offers modes of divine communication but little direct clarification of 8:10.
Makes explicit the paired inward effects around the angelic aid: strengthening and fear.
Provides a negative reversal of good news rather than support for its role in 8:10.
Links belief to heart-settling through a witnessed sign.
Its sorting and gathering imagery does not materially clarify the focus.
Reinforces that victory is God's action and not merely visible superiority.
The shared attributes add little after stronger source-of-victory parallels.
Adds a plea for a promised future, but only a remote parallel to the focus.
Generalizes divine help as a recurring outcome for earlier messengers.
Divine authority is too general to add much to 8:10.
Connects God-centered recitation, changing hearts, faith growth, and reliance.
Shows a plea for help answered through an unexpected material channel.
Does not add a usable connection to the focus's sign, hearts, or victory.
Places permitted numerical conflict and patient endurance alongside divine enabling.
Shows that purported helpers fail at crisis, sharpening exclusive reliance on God.
Heart-hardness is a remote contrary condition, without a focused link to 8:10.
Adds another impatience contrast, largely redundant with the earlier 27 cards.
Presents God's good news as the first disclosure of an enduring favorable outcome.
Shows divine support operating through human counteraction while God remains strong.
In the same conflict, contrasts reliance on God with cynical judgment about believers.
A bare plea for help contributes no further account of its source or effect.
Relates heart-settling to a confirming sign and testimony.
The following/rear relation is only a remote channel-level parallel.
A sound heart is relevant but does not explain the focus's reassurance or victory.
Denies that any alternative source can restore withdrawn capacities.
Adds an immediate ethical boundary for conduct within the same battle setting.
Shows ordinary patronal support failing, leaving divine mercy as the effective source.
Its account of unstable hearts and ambiguity only indirectly frames the focus.
Affirms sole divine judgment but offers little about the focus's process.
Sets patience under rejection until divine help arrives.
Uses the absence of good news as a contrary boundary rather than positive support.
Supplies the reluctant-believer setting immediately before the aid sequence.
Its ironic announcement of punishment is a contrast, not support for the focus.
Distinguishes reciprocal human support from the wider divine source and its limits.
The channel route is too remote and the text adds no focused connection.
Clarifies that human action can be an instrument without becoming the independent source.
A reliable divine promise is relevant only at a broad level.
In the same battle, exposes a false guarantee of protection that collapses at encounter.
Shows good news as an initiating divine disclosure, though outside the conflict setting.
Develops tranquility as a settled, return-ready condition rather than passivity.
The response to a call and subsequent plea are only a distant parallel.
Its punitive use of announcement is a contrary boundary, not positive support.
Does not materially clarify the focus.
Gives the focus's community a practical correlate: steadfastness and abundant remembrance.
Denies any protector or helper apart from God, reinforcing the source claim.
A generic favorable announcement adds little after closer good-news cards.
The gathering motif has no useful localized relation to 8:10.
Tests and denies the efficacy of alternative helpers and self-help.
Does not provide a sufficiently direct connection to the focus.
Adds divine management of perception in the same encounter to bring about the decree.
Treats good news as anticipatory, but repeats a point already better established.
Links trust in God amid affliction with a redirected heart.
Its life-cycle pattern and remote channels do not clarify 8:10.
Suggests protected return by divine favor, but only indirectly addresses the focus.
Shows a contrary process of hearts being diverted through secret talk.
Adds same-context commands against internal conflict, with patience under divine presence.
The loss of a helper is broadly relevant but redundant and distant.
Does not add a usable relation to the focus.
Prayer and response are relevant generally, but the channel evidence is remote.
Distinguishes coerced speech from an inwardly settled commitment.
Only repeats the attributes of might and wisdom without the focus's relation.
Directly precedes the encounter: a moderated vision prevents failure and dispute by divine saving.
Exposes a promised support network that cannot actually sustain aid.
The shared divine attributes alone add no focused clarification.
Shows the angelic force in the same sequence from the opposing side's experience.
States the asymmetry directly: divine help removes overcoming power, and its withdrawal leaves none.
Its inward-accountability theme is too distant from the focus.
Adds a later same-surah tactical consequence, but not the focus's central explanation.
Contrasts visible worldly movement with a reliable measure of outcome.
Directly parallels God as the one who joins hearts beyond human capacity.
In the same setting, names God as sufficient alongside the believing followers.
Frames good news and warning as complementary guidance rather than control of the outcome.
Remembrance and inward awareness are only a loose parallel.
Shows that claimed help is tested by whether it is enacted, not merely announced.
Sole divine judgment is broad background rather than a focused addition.
Provides a contrary image of hearts obscured by accumulated acts.
Parallels security after distress while also preserving the contrary self-concerned response.
Heart-sealing is an inverse boundary case, not positive support.
The demand for punishment repeats the impatience contrast without new leverage.
States that human conflict tests people and does not supply what divine power lacks.
Does not add a usable relation to the focus.
Eliminates both external helpers and self-rescue, sharpening the source contrast.
Pairs severe trial with the announced nearness of divine help.
Places overcoming a larger force under divine permission and patient endurance.
States that God supports with victory whom He wills in an armed encounter.
Directly identifies divine help at Badr despite apparent weakness.
Directly continues the Badr reassurance through promised angelic reinforcement.
Extends the angelic-reinforcement condition with patience and God-consciousness.
Names God as protector and best helper, strengthening the source claim.
Adds the counterpart inward operation: terror cast into opposing hearts.
Places the fulfillment of divine promise within the changing conditions of battle.
Shows a threatening report answered by reliance on God's sufficiency.
Names victory as coming from God within a contested communal setting.
Shows divine protection by restraining hostile hands and calls for reliance.
Connects allegiance to God with the victory of God's party.
Supplies a good-news-before-mercy pattern relevant to the focus's secondary rain reading.
Joins seeking God's help with patience when earthly outcome is unsettled.
Clarifies divine agency acting through human battle action, without making the human act independent.
Names God as sufficient and as the one who supports through aid and believers.
Adds the immediately adjacent relation of patient endurance, numbers, and divine presence.
Sets divine help in an actual battle against the failure of confidence in visible numbers.
Pairs tranquility with unseen forces and divine punishment in the same campaign sequence.
Frames reliance through the conviction that God's decree governs what reaches the community.
Denies any power apart from God to remove harm or repel His favor.
Shows help arriving to messengers at the point when ordinary expectation has narrowed.
Asks for supporting authority from God, making help a granted rather than self-generated capacity.
Provides another failure of group support and self-defense apart from God.
Shows divine response that removes distress after a direct appeal.
States divine defense of believers before the further support claim in 22:40.
Unites good news, mercy, and water from heaven, directly enriching the secondary rain reading.
Answers apparent entrapment with divine presence and guidance.
Connects response to the distressed with removal of harm.
Uses sent winds as good news before mercy, a close parallel to the secondary rain reading.
Explicitly presents helping believers as a divine commitment.
Recalls an assault answered by wind and unseen forces sent by God.
Shows the sight of opposing forces increasing believers in faith and submission.
Attributes the repelling of hostile forces and the believers' preservation to God.
Supplies the prior divine promise that frames the later statement of helped messengers.
Extends the promised-help sequence to God's host as the prevailing party.
Names God as sufficient for His servant against attempts to redirect fear and reliance.
Explicitly promises divine help to messengers and believers in worldly life and at testimony.
Combines angelic presence, freedom from fear and grief, and good news for the steadfast.
Reciprocally joins supporting God's cause with divine support and firm footing.
Pairs divine presence with the assurance that believers' deeds will not be diminished.
Directly links sent-down tranquility in believers' hearts with God's unseen forces.
Names the forces of the heavens and earth alongside God's might and wisdom.
Combines divine knowledge of hearts, sent-down tranquility, and a near victory.
Attributes the restraint of both sides' hands in the valley to God.
Sets divine tranquility upon messenger and believers against hostile fervor.
Places human support of God and His messengers within a test of what is unseen.
States the written divine determination that God and His messengers will prevail.
Attributes the casting of terror into opponents' hearts to God.
Contrasts believers' God-centered fear with the opponents' fragmented inward state.
Shows believers supporting God's cause and being supported to prevail over an enemy.
Connects reliance on God with His sufficiency when provision and outcome are not self-controlled.
